sources.note: PSI-20 detail record (local JSON): flightProgram 'International Space Station (ISS)'.

objective.value: Establish the burning conditions of condensed-phase fuels in a quiescent microgravity ambient as a function of material properties. Gaseous fuels (CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2) burn on porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter; O2/N2 ambients are examined across a range of pressures and oxygen concentrations, including the NASA-considered habitat atmospheres 14.7 psia at 21% O2, 10.2 psia at 26.5% O2 and 8.2 psia at 34% O2, with O2/CO2 ambients also desired, and extinction limits are determined.

sources.note: PSI-20 objective: wants to establish burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties, lists CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 on 25 and 50 mm porous circular burners, the three NASA atmospheres, O2/CO2 (desired) and extinction limits.
NASA ACME one-pager: unlike the other ACME experiments, BRE is focused on fire prevention, especially in spacecraft, to understand materials flammability and flammability test methods.
Challenge brief, 'Other investigations in PSI': BRE was a study of materials flammability.

safety_functions.note: Fire prevention via material selection / flammability screening.

sources.note: PSI-20 sub-research area 'Flames of Gaseous Fuels'; objective names gaseous CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 fuels.

fuel_phase.note: The actual fuel is gaseous. BRE emulates the burning of solid and liquid (condensed-phase) fuels with a gaseous fuel on a porous burner.

sources.note: PSI-20 objective names CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 mixtures; the experimental table lists 100% C2H4, 50% C2H4 and 100% CH4 fuel bottles.
ACME one-pager: a small number of gaseous fuels simulate burning of fuels such as paper, plastic and alcohol by matching surface temperature and smoke production.

fuel_materials.note: Fuels are the gases methane and ethylene (sometimes diluted with nitrogen). These emulate condensed fuels; paper/plastic/alcohol are the emulated analogues, not the actual fuel.

fuel_geometry.value: Flat porous circular burner, 25 mm and 50 mm diameters, fed with gaseous fuel to emulate condensed-phase burning.

sources.note: PSI-20 objective: porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter; the experimental table lists Burner Size (mm) 25 and 50.
ACME one-pager: BRE simulates solid and liquid fuel burning with a flat porous burner fed with gaseous fuel.
PSI-20 experimentHardware: 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'.
Challenge brief, 'Hardware': the six ACME experiments were conducted with the same modular hardware in the CIR.

apparatus.value: ACME modular hardware set: chamber insert with a flat porous burner (two heat-flux transducers and a surface thermocouple), a retracting resistively heated igniter, three mass flow controllers for fuel/oxidizer/inert/nitrogen, and an ACME avionics package.

sources.note: PSI-20 experimentHardware: ACME inert replaced the modular ACME hardware in the CIR.

ACME one-pager 'Burners and Igniter' / 'Gas Delivery': each BRE burner has two heat-flux transducers, most burners a surface thermocouple, internal porous-burner pressure is measured, and there are three mass flow controllers.
PSI PSI-20 experimental table PSI-20_Experimental table_ACME BRE.csv; per-test conditions, min and max of the listed columns

o2_percent.note: Range over 18 test rows of PSI-20_Experimental table_ACME BRE.csv, columns: Oxygen Conc (percent). Computed by scripts/psi_table_summary.py (initial conditions only). Check: Oxygen Conc (percent): as given; 2 value(s) dropped as impossible/ambiguous, e.g. 3400, 2100

sources.note: PSI-20 objective: NASA-considered habitat atmospheres to be examined are 14.7 psia/21% O2, 10.2 psia/26.5% O2 and 8.2 psia/34% O2.
PSI-20 experimental table note: chamber pressures were also varied but are not identified in the summary table.

pressure_psi.note: Range spans the three stated NASA atmospheres (8.2 to 14.7 psia). Medium confidence: the objective states these as the atmospheres to be examined and the summary table does not list per-test pressures.

sources.note: PSI-20 approach/objective describe burning in a quiescent microgravity ambient (no imposed flow).
Challenge brief: BRE was a study of materials flammability in still atmospheres.

airflow.note: Recorded as 0 cm/s (no imposed flow). The PSI-20 experimental table has no flow column, so this field is not script-overwritten. Quiescent ambient means no forced ventilation, not a measured zero velocity field.

sources.note: PSI-20 projectType is 'Microgravity Investigation'; the tests ran aboard the ISS.
PSI-20 objective: O2/N2 ambients with various pressures and O2 concentrations are examined, and the conditions are also to be considered for O2/CO2 ambients (desired).

diluents.note: Nitrogen diluent is used in the tested O2/N2 ambients (the table's oxygen concentrations are quoted as diluted with nitrogen); the O2/CO2 case is stated only as desired/planned.

value: Fuel dilution with nitrogen (100% vs 50% ethylene)

sources.note: PSI-20 experimental table: tests vary burner size (25/50 mm), fuel bottle (100% C2H4, 50% C2H4, 100% CH4) and oxygen concentration (listed 21, 25, 26.5, 34, 40%), and the table note says pressures were varied too.
PSI-20 objective: various pressures and ambient O2 concentrations, with diluent choice (N2 vs CO2) and fuel mixtures varied.

value: Quiescent ambient (no imposed airflow / no forced ventilation)

sources.note: PSI-20 approach: for each test the chamber contents are set (diluent, O2 concentration, pressure) and the flame is observed without changing the fuel flow rate; the ambient is quiescent.

held_constant.note: The ambient is held quiescent across tests. Fuel flow is not strictly constant: it is controlled from the measured burner heat flux and surface temperature to emulate condensed-phase vaporization, and is stepped down to find extinction.

value: Heat-flux transducers at the burner (two per BRE burner)
Color video cameras (high-definition digital and analog)
Gas chromatograph for chamber-atmosphere analysis (O2, N2, CO2, CO, fuel gases)

sources.note: ACME one-pager: each BRE burner has two heat-flux transducers, burners carry a surface thermocouple and internal pressure measurement; ACME uses radiometers, color/CH*/OH* cameras, a gas chromatograph and SAMS-II acceleration measurement.
PSI-20 approach: burner surface temperature and heat flux are measured, with a heat-flux sensor having a temperature limit.

relevance_notes.value: Named in the challenge brief as a materials-flammability investigation even though it burned gaseous fuel. BRE is the one ACME experiment focused on spacecraft fire prevention: it observed quasi-steady burning of condensed-fuel analogues (e.g. PMMA, Nylon) in microgravity even with no air flow, notably in elevated-oxygen atmospheres, and assesses whether existing material flammability test methods are valid for low and partial gravity.

sources.note: Challenge brief, 'Other investigations in PSI': BRE studied materials flammability in still atmospheres as a function of material properties.

PSI-20 researchImpacts: quasi-steady burning of condensed-phase materials (PMMA, Nylon) in microgravity without air flow, ongoing combustion in elevated-oxygen atmospheres while the 21% O2 case self-extinguished.

value: Improved material flammability screening: BRE results suggest increased use of a cone calorimeter (NASA Test 2) to measure material properties matching the microgravity flames.

sources.note: PSI-20 researchImpacts: BRE results suggest NASA may want to increase use of its alternative flammability Test 2 with the cone calorimeter.

earth_applications.note: Inferred: the cone calorimeter cited in the impacts is an Earth fire-test instrument, so the recommendation implies a terrestrial material-testing benefit; the impacts text itself frames the benefit for spacecraft.

notes: Local PSI sources used: data/source/psi/PSI-20.json, PSI-20.search.json and the conditions table data/source/psi/tables/PSI-20.csv. No psi.nasa.gov page was fetched (JavaScript), so none is claimed.

conditions.o2_percent is left at the seed value (null) on purpose: the PSI-20 table has an 'Oxygen Conc (percent)' column, so scripts/psi_apply_conditions.py overwrites it (table min 21%, max 40%). The raw table also contains two impossible values, 3400% and 2100%, which are data-entry errors.

conditions.pressure_psi is recorded from the PSI-20 objective (three NASA atmospheres, 8.2-14.7 psia); medium confidence because the summary table states pressures were varied but does not list them per test.
conditions.airflow is recorded as 0 cm/s (quiescent ambient). The PSI-20 table has no flow column, so it is not script-overwritten; treat 0 as 'no imposed flow', not a measured field.

Data files: PSI-20 lists one file, 'PSI-20_Experimental table_ACME BRE.csv' (1,113 bytes); a metadata asset 'PSI-20_metadata_PSI-96_ACME BRE.zip' is also listed. PSI reports totalFileSize about 2,035,568,427,496 bytes (~2 TB) for the investigation; nothing was downloaded.
The ACME NASA one-pager calls ACME 'five' then 'six' independent experiments; the brief says six. shared_with lists all five other ACME experiments including acme-flame-design (PSI-10).

Partial gravity: the ACME one-pager says BRE assesses flammability test methods for low AND partial-gravity environments, but PSI-20 is a Microgravity (0 g) investigation and PSI holds no partial-gravity combustion data; gravity_g is 0 g and no partial-gravity value is implied.
publications: the first six of the 16 entries in the PSI-20 record were recorded with their DOI links; the rest were omitted only for brevity, not for lack of source.
